exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Long Answer Questions — Q5
exercises.problem:
Identify the type of chemical reaction in the following statements and define each of them :
(a) Digestion of food in our body
(b) Rusting of iron
(c) Heating of manganese dioxide with aluminium powder
(d) Blue colour of copper sulphate solution disappears when iron fillings are added to it
(e) Dilute hydrochloric acid is added to sodium hydroxide solution to form sodium chloride and water.
exercises.solution:
(a) Decomposition reaction : Carbohydrates are broken down to form glucose. Complex molecule broken down into simpler molecule during the digestion of food. Therefore it is a decomposition reaction.
(b) Redox reaction
Oxidation : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
Reduction : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo></mrow></msup><mi>⟶</mi><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
Overall : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><mn>2</mn><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
(c) Displacement reaction
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mi>⟶</mi><mn>3</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
Aluminium being higher in reactivity series displaces Mn from its compound. Therefore it is an example of displacement reaction.
(d) Displacement reaction
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mi>⟶</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></mrow></mrow></math>
Iron is placed at higher position than copper in reactivity series. Therefore iron displace copper from copper sulphate solution which result in the formation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> leaving behind copper.
(e) Neutralisation reaction
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mi>⟶</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi></mrow></math>
NaOH which is a base react with hydrochloric acid leads to formation of sodium chloride (salt) and water. This is an example of neutralisation reaction.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Reasoning Based Questions — Q1
exercises.problem: Why is photosynthesis considered as an endothermic reaction?
exercises.solution: Photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction because light energy in the form of sun light is absorbed during the process by green plants.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Reasoning Based Questions — Q2
exercises.problem: Why is the amount of gas collected in one of the test tubes in electrolysis of water double of the amount collected in the other? Name this gas.
exercises.solution: It is because on electrolysis water decomposes to form hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> by volume. The gas with double volume is hydrogen.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Reasoning Based Questions — Q3
exercises.problem: The oxidation of iron to rust is a problem, but the oxidation of aluminium to aluminium oxide is not why?
exercises.solution: Iron is oxidized in presence of atmospheric oxygen and water to form iron oxide trihydrate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>·</mo><mn>3</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, known as rust. It peels off iron surface exposing fresh iron surface for further rusting. While, aluminium, oxidized in presence of atmospheric oxygen to form a thin, transparent and non water-soluble layer of aluminium oxide <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, which shield the metal from further oxidation and maintains its metallic shine. Hence, the oxidation of iron to rust is a problem for structural engineers but the oxidation of aluminium is not.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Reasoning Based Questions — Q4
exercises.problem: Why the green colour of ferrous sulphate salt changes to brown and produces smell of burning sulphur on strong heating?
exercises.solution:
Decomposition reaction
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><munder><mrow><mn>2</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mover><mstyle scriptlevel="0"><mo>→</mo></mstyle><mpadded width="+0.833em" lspace="0.556em" voffset="-.2em" height="-.2em"><mrow><mi>Δ</mi></mrow><mspace depth=".25em" /></mpadded></mover><munder><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mtext> (brown) </mtext></mrow></munder><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mtext> (green) </mtext></mrow></munder></mrow></math>
Smell of sulphur is due to the formation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> gases.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Reasoning Based Questions — Q5
exercises.problem: Why colourless lead nitrate produces a yellow residue and brown fumes on heating?
exercises.solution: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><munder><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mtext> (colourless) </mtext></mrow></munder><mover><mstyle scriptlevel="0"><mo>→</mo></mstyle><mpadded width="+0.833em" lspace="0.556em" voffset="-.2em" height="-.2em"><mrow><mi>Δ</mi></mrow><mspace depth=".25em" /></mpadded></mover><munder><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mtext> (yellow) </mtext></mrow></munder><mo>+</mo><munder><mrow><mn>4</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mtext> (brown fumes) </mtext></mrow></munder><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Reasoning Based Questions — Q6
exercises.problem: When an aqueous solution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is added to common salt solution, then a white precipitate is formed. Why?
exercises.solution:
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> white ppt.
Double displacement reaction.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Reasoning Based Questions — Q7
exercises.problem: Why the formation of black precipitate takes place, when hydrogen sulphide gas is passed through an aqueous solution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ?
exercises.solution:
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> Black ppt.
Double displacement reaction.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Reasoning Based Questions — Q8
exercises.problem: Why sodium metal reacts violently with water?
exercises.solution: Reaction between sodium metal and water is highly exothermic. During the course of the reaction hydrogen gas produces which catches fire easily.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Reasoning Based Questions — Q9
exercises.problem: Why antioxidants are added to fat and oil containing food?
exercises.solution: When antioxidants are added to food, they act as reducing agent. Therefore the fat and oil present in the food do not get oxidised easily consequently prevent rancidity.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Reasoning Based Questions — Q10
exercises.problem: Why magnesium ribbon burns in air with a dazzling flame and forms white ash?
exercises.solution: When magnesium ribbon burns in air, addition of oxygen to magnesium takes place to produce magnesium oxide. This process accompanied with the evolution of heat and light due to which dazzling flame observed.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — HOTS Questions — Q1
exercises.problem: A substance X , which is an oxide of a group 2 element, is used intensively in the cement industry. This element is present in bones also. On treatment with water it forms a solution which turns red litmus blue. Identify <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> and also write the chemical reactions involved.
exercises.solution:
Substance calcium oxide.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> turns red litmus blue.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — HOTS Questions — Q2
exercises.problem: A solution of KBr is mixed with a solution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. Predict what happens.
exercises.solution: The four ions involved are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>K</mi><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math>. An exchange of ions produces the compounds <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. Both of these compounds are soluble, so no reaction occurs.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — HOTS Questions — Q3
exercises.problem:
Identify the reducing agent in the following reactions.
(a) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>4</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>⟶</mi><mn>4</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi></mrow></math>
(b) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>⟶</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></mrow></mrow></math>
(c) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mi>⟶</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
(d) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>⟶</mi><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi></mrow></math>
exercises.solution:
(a) Ammonia <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
(b) Water <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> act as reducing agents
(c) Carbon monoxide (CO)
(d) Hydrogen
Hint-Reducing agents are those substances which have the ability of adding hydrogen or removing oxygen from the other substances.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — HOTS Questions — Q4
exercises.problem:
Write balanced equations for the reactions between each of the following oxides and water :
(a) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi></mrow></math>
(b) CaO
(c) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
exercises.solution:
(a) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mi>⟶</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow></mrow></math>
(b) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mi>⟶</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
(c) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mi>⟶</mi><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — HOTS Questions — Q5
exercises.problem: Represent the following chemical reaction as a balanced equation. Liquid "rubbing alcohol," <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> reacts with oxygen to form carbon dioxide gas and water.
exercises.solution:
First, represent the name of the species involved as reactants and products with formulae and indicate their physical states.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
Next, balance carbon. Place a coefficient of 3 in front of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> to balance the carbons in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi></mrow></math>. Balance the eight hydrogens in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi></mrow></math> by adding a coefficient of 4 in front of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi></mrow></math>.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><mn>3</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
Now note that there are 10 oxygens on the right. On the left, one oxygen is in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi></mrow></math> so nine are needed from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. To get an odd number of oxygens from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> we need to use a fractional coefficient, in this case <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> (i.e., <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>×</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></math> )
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><mn>3</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
Finally, we need to clear the fraction so that all coefficients are whole numbers. Multiply the whole equation by 2 and do a quick check.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><mn>6</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — HOTS Questions — Q6
exercises.problem:
(a) Would you expect aluminum oxide to be a solid, liquid, or gas at room temperature?
(b) Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction of aluminum oxide with nitric acid.
exercises.solution:
(a) Because aluminum oxide is the oxide of a metal, we would expect it to be an ionic solid. Indeed it is, and it has a very high melting point, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>2072</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>.
(b) In its compounds, aluminum has a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></math> charge, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, the oxide ion is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, consequently, the formula of aluminum oxide is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. Metal oxides tend to be basic and therefore reacts with acids to form salts and water. In this case the salt formed is aluminum nitrate, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. The balanced chemical equation is
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — HOTS Questions — Q7
exercises.problem:
Consider the following two possible reactions. If a reaction does occur, write the balanced equations illustrating the reactions.
(a) A strip of tin metal is placed in an aqueous <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> solution.
(b) A strip of silver metal is placed in an aqueous perchloric acid solution.
exercises.solution:
In the activity series that Sn is higher in the series than Ag . Therefore Sn replaces <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></math> ions from solution.
(a) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
(b) In the activity series, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is in higher position than Ag . Therefore, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> replaces <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, but the reverse reaction, the replacement of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math>by Ag , does not occur. No reaction occurs.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — HOTS Questions — Q8
exercises.problem:
Write combination reactions that occur when the metal barium reacts with the following nonmetals.
(a) Hydrogen
(b) Sulfur
(c) Bromine
(d) Nitrogen
exercises.solution:
(a) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
(b) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>8</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><mn>8</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
(c) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
(d) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Questions — Q1
exercises.problem: Why should a magnesium ribbon be cleaned before burning in air?
exercises.solution: Magnesium ribbon has a coating of basic magnesium carbonate on its surface, which is formed by a slow action of moist air on it. Therefore before burning it in air, it is cleaned by a sand paper which removes the protective layer of basic magnesium carbonate from the surface of magnesium ribbon, so that it can easily burn.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Questions — Q2
exercises.problem:
Write the balanced equation for the following chemical reactions.
(i) Hydrogen + Chlorine ⟶ Hydrogen chloride
(ii) Barium chloride + Aluminium sulphate ⟶ Barium sulphate + Aluminium chloride
(iii) Sodium + Water ⟶
Sodium hydroxide + Hydrogen
exercises.solution:
(i) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
(ii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi></mrow></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
(iii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Questions — Q3
exercises.problem:
Write a balanced chemical equation with state symbols for the following reactions.
(i) Solutions of barium chloride and sodium sulphate in water react to give insoluble barium sulphate and the solution of sodium chloride.
(ii) Sodium hydroxide solution (in water) reacts with hydrochloric acid solution (in water) to produce sodium chloride solution and water.
exercises.solution:

exercises.solution: The gases formed at two electrodes are produced due to decomposition of water on passing electricity. Since the electrolysis of water produces 2 volume of hydrogen gas and 1 volume of oxygen gas, thus we can say that the ratio of hydrogen and oxygen in water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>:</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> by volume and hence the amount of gas collected in one test tube will be double of the amount collected in other.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Questions — Q6
exercises.problem: Why does the colour of copper sulphate solution changes when an iron nail is dipped in it?
exercises.solution:
As iron is more reactive than copper thus it displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><munder><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mtext> (Blue) </mtext></mrow></munder><mo>+</mo><munder><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mtext> (Green) </mtext></mrow></munder><mi>⟶</mi><munder><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></munder><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
In this way concentration of copper sulphate decreases while concentration of ferrous sulphate increases. As a result colour changes from blue to green.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Exercise — Q4
exercises.problem: What is a balanced chemical equation? Why should chemical equations be balanced?
exercises.solution:
Balanced chemical equation: - A chemical equation is said to be balanced if the number of atoms of each element participating in the reaction are equal on both
side of the equation. The chemical reaction should be balanced because law of conservation of mass states that 'In a chemical reaction total mass of the reactant must be equal to the total mass of the product'.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Exercise — Q9
exercises.problem: What does one mean by exothermic and endothermic reaction? Give examples.
exercises.solution:
Exothermic reaction : - Those reactions which occur with the evolution of heat are exothermic reactions. e.g. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><munderover><mstyle scriptlevel="0"><mo>→</mo></mstyle><mpadded width="+0.833em" lspace="0.556em" voffset="-.2em" height="-.2em"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mtext> heat </mtext></mrow><mspace depth=".25em" /></mpadded><mpadded width="+0.833em" lspace="0.556em" voffset="-.2em" height="-.2em"><mrow /><mspace depth=".25em" /></mpadded></munderover></mrow></math>
Endothermic reaction : - Those reactions which occur with the absorption of heat are endothermic reactions. e.g.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mover><mstyle scriptlevel="0"><mo>→</mo></mstyle><mpadded width="+0.833em" lspace="0.556em" voffset="-.2em" height="-.2em"><mrow><mtext> heat </mtext></mrow><mspace depth=".25em" /></mpadded></mover><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Exercise — Q10
exercises.problem: Why is respiration considered an exothermic reaction? Explain.
exercises.solution:
Respiration is the most important biochemical reaction which releases energy in the cell. When we breathe air (oxygen) enters into our lungs and oxygen binds itself to haemoglobin present in red blood cells (RBC). It is then carried to million of cells present in our body. Respiration occurs in these cells and is accompanied by the combustion of glucose <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>12</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> producing carbon dioxide ( <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> ) and water ( <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi></mrow></math> ). A large amount of energy is released in this chemical reaction.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>6</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2820</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></mrow></mrow></math>
Since the process is accompanied by release of energy so it is considered as an exothermic reaction.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Exercise — Q11
exercises.problem: Why are decomposition reactions called the opposite of combination reactions? Write equations for these reactions.
exercises.solution:
During decomposition reaction a single reactant decompose to form two or more products, whereas in combination reaction two or more reactants react to form a single product. e.g.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>⟶</mi><mn>2</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> (Combination reaction)
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mover><mstyle scriptlevel="0"><mo>→</mo></mstyle><mpadded width="+0.833em" lspace="0.556em" voffset="-.2em" height="-.2em"><mrow><mi>Δ</mi></mrow><mspace depth=".25em" /></mpadded></mover><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> (Decomposition reaction)

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Exercise — Q12
exercises.problem: What is the difference between displacement and double displacement reactions? Write equations for these reactions.
exercises.solution:
Displacement reaction : - In this reaction an element which is more reactive displaces the other element which is less reactive from its salt solution. e.g.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
Double displacement reaction : - In this reaction exchange of ions between two reactants takes place. e.g.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Exercise — Q13
exercises.problem: In the refining of silver, the recovery of silver from silver nitrate solution involved displacement by copper metal. Write down the reaction involved.
exercises.solution: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Exercise — Q14
exercises.problem: What do you mean by a precipitation reaction? Explain by giving examples.
exercises.solution: Those reactions which produce an insoluble product or precipitate are known as precipitation reaction. e.g. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>↓</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Exercise — Q15
exercises.problem: A shiny brown coloured element ' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> ' on heating in air becomes black in colour. Name the element ' X ' and the black coloured compound formed.
exercises.solution: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><munder><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></mrow></mrow><mrow><mtext> brown </mtext></mrow></munder><mo>+</mo><munder><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mtext> from air </mtext></mrow></munder><mover><mstyle scriptlevel="0"><mo>→</mo></mstyle><mpadded width="+0.833em" lspace="0.556em" voffset="-.2em" height="-.2em"><mrow><mi>Δ</mi></mrow><mspace depth=".25em" /></mpadded></mover><munder><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow></mrow><mrow><mtext> Cuprous Oxide </mtext></mrow></munder></mrow></math> (Black)

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Exercise — Q16
exercises.problem: Why do we apply paint on iron articles?
exercises.solution: To prevent iron articles from rusting, we apply paint on it, by which iron does not come in contact with air and moisture which causes rusting.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Exercise — Q17
exercises.problem: Oil and fat containing food items are flushed with nitrogen. Why?
exercises.solution: When the oil and fat containing food is surrounded by unreactive gas nitrogen, oxygen become unavailable to cause oxidation and therefore prevent rancidity.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Exercise — Q18
exercises.problem:
Explain the following terms with one example each.
(a) Corrosion
(b) Rancidity
exercises.solution:
Corrosion : - It is a process in which metals are eaten up gradually by the action of air, moisture or a chemical on their surface. For example rusting of iron.
Rancidity - When fat and oil containing food is oxidised with air or oxygen, their smell and taste changes. This process is called rancidity.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Text - Book Exercise — Q19
exercises.problem: Write chemical equation for decomposition reactions where energy is supplied in the form of (i) heat (ii) light (iii) electricity.
exercises.solution:
(i) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mover><mstyle scriptlevel="0"><mo>→</mo></mstyle><mpadded width="+0.833em" lspace="0.556em" voffset="-.2em" height="-.2em"><mrow><mtext> heat </mtext></mrow><mspace depth=".25em" /></mpadded></mover><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
(ii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mover><mstyle scriptlevel="0"><mo>→</mo></mstyle><mpadded width="+0.833em" lspace="0.556em" voffset="-.2em" height="-.2em"><mrow><mtext> sunlight </mtext></mrow><mspace depth=".25em" /></mpadded></mover><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>
(iii) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mover><mstyle scriptlevel="0"><mo>→</mo></mstyle><mpadded width="+0.833em" lspace="0.556em" voffset="-.2em" height="-.2em"><mrow><mtext> electricity </mtext></mrow><mspace depth=".25em" /></mpadded></mover><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>

(a) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>→</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
(b) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>4</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>→</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi></mrow></math>
(c) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><msub><mi>O</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>→</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Multiple Choice Questions — Q2
exercises.problem:
When hydrogen sulphide gas is passed through a blue solution of copper sulphate, a black precipitate of copper sulphide is obtained and the sulphuric acid so formed remains in the solution. The reaction is an example of -
(a) a combination reaction
(b) a displacement reaction
(c) a decomposition reaction
(d) a double decomposition reaction

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Multiple Choice Questions — Q3
exercises.problem:
What happens when copper rod is dipped in iron sulphate solution?
(a) Copper displaces iron
(b) Blue colour of copper sulphate solution is obtained
(c) No reaction takes place
(d) Reaction is exothermic
exercises.solution: (c) Iron is more reactive than copper, hence Cu will not displace iron from iron sulphate, hence no reaction will take place.

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Multiple Choice Questions — Q4
exercises.problem:

(a) The zinc surface became dull and black.
(b) A gas evolved which burns with a pop sound.
(c) The solution remained colourless.
(d) The solution becomes green in colour.
exercises.solution:
40 g CO is formed from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>100</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>44</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>×</mo><mn>44</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>
If mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is 10 g , then weight of empty test tube <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>30.08</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>10.0</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>20.08</mn><mrow><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow></mrow></math>

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Multiple Choice Questions — Q5
exercises.problem:

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mi>⟶</mi></mrow></math> no reaction

The equation
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>→</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">(</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>O</mi></mrow></math>

exercises.title: Assertion \& Reason — Multiple Choice Questions — Q8
exercises.problem:
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Z</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo></mrow></math> dil <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>⟶</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Z</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>↑</mo></mrow></math> Above reaction is -

exercises.problem:
The reaction in which two compounds exchange their ions to form two new compounds is -
(a) a displacement reaction
(b) a decomposition reaction

(d) a double displacement reaction
exercises.solution:
The oxidation number of Mn in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is-
